name: Taipei
title: Holidays in Taipei
intro: Night markets, mountain temples and hot springs on the edge of a friendly, easy-going city, with green hills right on the metro. Here's what Taipei is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The Taipei 101 tower rising above the city skyline at sunset, seen from a green hillside with pampas grass

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 7 hrs ahead of the UK (8 in winter)

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 90 days

facts_note: You must fill in the Taiwan Arrival Card online within three days before you arrive. Bring an adaptor for flat two-pin plugs, and check GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: October, November and April are the best months, warm and mostly clear for walking the city and the hills. July and August are very hot and humid, often 34°C or more, with typhoons possible from June to October. May and June bring the 'plum rains'. Winter is mild but often grey and damp, with the Lantern Festival lighting up the city around February.

things.name: Taipei 101
things.blurb: The landmark tower, with a fast lift to the observatory and its huge wind damper on show inside.

things.name: Elephant Mountain
things.blurb: A short, steep climb from the metro to the classic view over Taipei 101 and the city, best at sunset.

things.name: Night markets
things.blurb: Shilin, Raohe and Ningxia night markets for bubble tea, dumplings, pepper buns and plenty more.

things.name: National Palace Museum
things.blurb: One of the world's great collections of Chinese art, from jade and bronzes to porcelain and paintings.

things.name: Beitou hot springs
things.blurb: Soak in hot-spring baths in a leafy valley at the end of a metro line, with a free hot-springs museum.

things.name: Maokong Gondola
things.blurb: A cable car up to hillside tea houses, with views back over the city.

things.name: Jiufen
things.blurb: A hillside old gold-mining town of lantern-lit lanes and tea houses above the sea, about an hour away.

faqs.question: How do you get to Taipei from the UK?
faqs.answer: EVA Air flies direct from London Heathrow. Otherwise connect through a hub such as Hong Kong, Singapore or Dubai.

faqs.question: Is Taipei easy to get around?
faqs.answer: Yes. The metro is clean, cheap and signed in English, and an EasyCard covers trains, buses and even some shops.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Taipei?
faqs.answer: Four or five days covers the city, a night market or two and a hot spring. A week lets you add Jiufen and other day trips.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Taipei?
faqs.answer: Spring and autumn are best, especially October and November. Summer is very hot and humid, with typhoons possible.
